rationale: Seven numerical-passing, compiling observations, all with actual smem pinned at 32768 bytes (the hard portability cap). Best remains 64x128x32 with stages=2 (attempt-02 swizzle=16, attempt-05 swizzle=8) at 399.54 us. Simulated DRAM is flat at 16.78 MB in every run, so the analytical serpentine panel-reuse traffic term has NOT materialized as measured traffic; matched-tile comparisons (attempt-01 vs 04 at 64x128x64 st=1, both 402.23 us; attempt-03 vs 06 at 64x128x32 st=1, both 408.93 us) show swizzle has no measurable latency or DRAM effect. The remaining untested matched comparison is swizzle=0 vs 16 at the best config (64x128x32, stages=2); we keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] one more round so HiGHS can run that disambiguation at the best tile/stage. We keep all tile/stage domains full because the 32KB cap has forced every selection to num_stages 1-2, and no configuration with stages=3 has yet been evaluated; smaller block_M/block_N with block_K=32 could unlock stages=3 within the cap, and deeper staging at small block_K is the clearest observed lever (stages=2 beat stages=1 at 64x128x32). Weights carried from attempts 05-06: traffic down to 0.75 because the analytic reuse term is unreliable and measured DRAM is flat; pipeline 2.5 to prioritize the empirically useful lever; footprint 0.5 because the hard cap already enforces memory pressure and extra weight only distorts ranking; launches 1 to avoid overfitting seven points. If this round again shows no swizzle effect at matched config, narrow swizzle to [0] and shift exploration toward stages=3 tiles. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.
